scope: Recipient-specific operational email checks; user authorization is separate from recipient consent
operationalOptOutAction: Suppress immediately when observed and before additional sending

routes: verified Spam Act Schedule 2 clause 4 conspicuous-publication conditions
publicationChecks: official conspicuous publication attributable to account-holder/organisation
exact pitch relevant to the published role/function
requirements: identify sender and usable contact
functional free email unsubscribe
honour withdrawal within five business days; campaign suppresses upon observation
countries.decision: Evidence must satisfy a specific route; a public generic mailbox does not automatically qualify. No marketing email requesting permission to evade consent.

routes: individual commercial-email first pitch complying with CAN-SPAM
requirements: truthful From/Reply-To/subject
visible advertisement identification
actual valid postal address
clear free reply-based opt-out
honour opt-out within ten business days; campaign suppresses upon observation
countries.decision: Verify identity, role/offer fit, suppressions and all required commercial-email content. No prior recipient interest or consent is inferred.

routes: verified deemed consent from conspicuous business/official publication
publicationChecks: public business/official address published by recipient or organisation
no accompanying refusal of unsolicited commercial messages
exact pitch relevant to recipient business/role/functions/duties
requirements: clearly identify business and usable contact
clear free email unsubscribe facility
honour unsubscribe within five working days; campaign suppresses upon observation
countries.decision: Record source, date, refusal check and exact business-role relevance before relying on deemed consent. No harvested/purchased lists.

routes: verified applicable implied consent including qualifying conspicuous publication
publicationChecks: direct public publication by or caused by account-holder/recipient
exact pitch relevant to recipient business/role/functions/duties
preserve where/when found and relevance evidence
requirements: identify sender and represented business
mailing address and usable contact valid at least sixty days
clear free unsubscribe valid at least sixty days
honour unsubscribe within ten business days; campaign suppresses upon observation
countries.decision: No broad right to email any public address. Assess each direct publication and exact message; copied third-party lists are insufficient.

routes: Verified corporate-subscriber business email under PECR, plus UK GDPR lawful basis where personal data is processed
Documented valid consent or verified applicable soft opt-in for individual subscribers
publicationChecks: Verify actual legal entity and corporate/individual subscriber category; published address alone is insufficient
Official relevant business contact and exact offer relevance
Inspect accompanying contact/privacy/terms restrictions and all shared user/recipient exclusions
Where personal data is used, document purpose/necessity/balancing legitimate-interests assessment and required privacy information
requirements: Do not conceal sender identity
Valid free reply-based opt-out and usable contact
Suppress objections immediately across both mailboxes and all campaigns
No tracking pixels; minimise personal data
Treat uncertain legal form/category as individual subscriber; hold unless consent/soft opt-in route proven
countries.decision: Corporate-subscriber email does not require PECR consent, but does not remove UK GDPR duties or exclusions. Sole traders and some partnerships need valid consent or applicable soft opt-in; no cold permission-request workaround. Prefer verified corporate bodies and generic business-role routes; hold unclear identities or missing route. Current ICO guidance notes review following Data (Use and Access) Act; recheck before a new pitch.

historicalMiddleEastStatus: No new pitches after explicit four-country scope clarification on 12 October 2026; preserve history and monitor replies
